q: A Deployment has `replicas: 4`, `maxSurge: 25%`, `maxUnavailable: 25%`. During a rolling update, what are the maximum total pods and the minimum available pods?
explain: maxSurge rounds up (25% of 4 = 1, so at most 5 pods) and maxUnavailable rounds down (1, so at least 3 available).

q: You run `kubectl scale deploy api --replicas=6`. Does this create a new revision in `kubectl rollout history`?
options: No, only changes to `spec.template` create a new ReplicaSet/revision
Yes, every spec change creates a revision
Only when using the Recreate strategy
explain: Scaling changes `replicas` on the current ReplicaSet. New revisions come from pod template changes (image, env, resources, template labels/annotations).

q: A new release has a bug that makes `/readyz` return 503. The Deployment uses `maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 1`. What happens?
options: All pods are replaced and users see errors
Kubernetes automatically rolls back to the previous ReplicaSet
One new pod is created, never becomes Ready, old pods keep serving, and after `progressDeadlineSeconds` the rollout is marked failed
explain: The controller can surge one pod but cannot remove old pods until new ones are available. Progress stalls and the `Progressing` condition becomes False with `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`. There is no automatic rollback; run `kubectl rollout undo` or fix forward.

q: When should you use the `Recreate` strategy?
options: For every stateless API to save resources
When two versions cannot run at the same time, e.g. a single-writer ReadWriteOnce volume or an incompatible schema
explain: Recreate stops all old pods before starting new ones. You accept a short outage in exchange for never running two versions concurrently.

q: What does a StatefulSet guarantee? (select all)
options: A PVC per pod from `volumeClaimTemplates`, re-attached when the pod is recreated
Automatic database replication and failover between replicas
Ordered creation and deletion by default
explain: StatefulSets provide identity, per-pod storage and ordering. Replication, failover and backups are the application's or an operator's job (e.g. CloudNativePG), or use a managed database.

q: What DNS name resolves to the second pod of StatefulSet `kafka` (serviceName `kafka-headless`) in namespace `data`?
explain: Ordinals start at 0, so the second pod is `kafka-1`. Per-pod records have the form `<pod>.<governing headless service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`.

q: You scale a StatefulSet from 3 to 1 replicas with default settings, then back to 3. What happens to `data-db-1` and `data-db-2`?
options: They are deleted on scale-down and recreated empty
They are retained on scale-down and re-attached to `db-1` and `db-2` on scale-up
They are moved to the ReplicaSet
explain: `persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy` defaults to `Retain` for both `whenScaled` and `whenDeleted`, so data is kept and re-used by the pod with the same ordinal.

q: A CronJob runs every 5 minutes, but a run sometimes takes 8 minutes and overlapping runs corrupt data. Which setting fixes the overlap?
explain: `Forbid` skips a scheduled run while the previous Job is still active. `parallelism` applies within one Job, not across Jobs created by the CronJob. Also make the job idempotent, since CronJobs are at-least-once.

q: Which statements about Jobs are true? (select all)
options: `restartPolicy: Always` is not allowed in a Job's pod template
With `restartPolicy: Never`, each retry creates a new pod
`backoffLimit` is the number of retries before the Job is marked Failed
A Job with `completionMode: Indexed` gives each pod a `JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX` env var
explain: Jobs allow only `Never` or `OnFailure`. `Never` keeps failed pods for inspection and creates new ones. After `backoffLimit` failures the Job gets `BackoffLimitExceeded`. Indexed Jobs expose the index for static sharding.

q: Where should shipit's database migrations run when the API Deployment has 6 replicas?
options: In an init container of the API pods
In a Job (or a pre-deploy hook) that runs once before the rollout, with backward-compatible schema changes
explain: Init containers would run the migration in all 6 pods concurrently and on every restart. A single Job runs it once. Expand/contract migrations keep old and new pods compatible during the rollout.

q: You need a log collector on every node, including newly added nodes. Which controller?
options: Deployment with `replicas` equal to node count
explain: A DaemonSet runs one pod per eligible node and automatically adds pods to new nodes. Add tolerations if it must also run on tainted nodes like control-plane nodes.

q: You implement a canary with Service selector `app=shop`, Deployment `shop-stable` (8 replicas) and `shop-canary` (2 replicas). Roughly what share of new connections go to the canary?
options: It depends on which Deployment was created first
explain: The Service load-balances across all Ready pods matching the selector, roughly uniformly per connection: 2 of 10 pods is about 20%. For precise weights use Gateway API HTTPRoute weights, a mesh, or Argo Rollouts.

q: A hotfix was rolled back with `kubectl rollout undo`, but 10 minutes later the broken version is back. The team uses Argo CD. Why?
options: The HPA re-applied the old template
GitOps synced the Deployment back to what git declares; the rollback must be a git revert
explain: `rollout undo` changes the live object, creating drift from git. The GitOps controller reconciles live state back to git. Roll back by reverting the commit.
